title: Nontransitive random decks
notes: Keep one adult at each table. For K-1 Problems 1-3, split the pictured pairs among the children and pool a complete shared nine-pair page for each comparison. Then bring the three comparisons together to check the cycle; each child need not make 27 records. On return, K-1 can play the advantage game (P4), change one card or swap (P5-6), then try P7-8 if ready. Grades 2-3 also share and pool comparisons for P1 and new arrangements in P3; P2 uses short draws without another exhaustive tally. On return they can choose altered decks, duplication or exact totals (P3-6). Grades 4-5 can choose one complete search, duplication comparison or two-card obstruction (P2-7) as its own visit.
